Elaine / Tom —

Appreciate the questionnaire. I've filled the attached PDF and provided concise answers below; I've also included links to our SOC 2 and data residency docs for quick reference. If you'd like, we can book a 30-min walkthrough with our security team.

Q1: Where is customer request/response content stored and for how long?
A1: By default Redwood's hosted API processes request/response content in-memory for inference and does not persist user-provided prompt/content to our long-term production dataset. We maintain short-lived operational logs (request metadata, model selection, latency traces) used for debugging and billing, retained for up to 30 days by default. If a customer explicitly opts into longer storage (for fine-tuning, audit logging, or analytics), those artifacts are stored in the customer's selected region and retention period is configurable.

Q2: How are erasure (data subject) requests handled? Timelines & scope?
A2: For hosted API customers we support the following:
- Customer-initiated erasure: We remove customer-stored artifacts and indices from active stores within 72 hours and purge related items from replicas/backups on the next scheduled snapshot lifecycle (typically within 30 days).
- Customer may request a full verification attestation once purge completes.
- Note: Ephemeral inference inputs that were never persisted beyond transient logs are covered in our retention policy above; where retention >0 days is enabled, we will remove those records on request per the timeline above.

Q3: Backups and snapshots? Cross-region replication?
A3: Persistent customer artifacts (when enabled) are snapshotted daily and retained according to the customer's retention setting. Backups may be replicated across regions only when the customer selects multi-region replication; by default we keep data in the customer-selected region for single-region customers. Restoration procedures and retention of snapshots are documented in our Backup & DR runbook.

Q4: Can data be pinned to a single jurisdiction?
A4: Yes — for enterprise accounts we offer geo-fencing: data at rest and backups remain in the selected jurisdiction (US, EU, APAC) and are prevented from being replicated outside that boundary. Hosted API self-serve customers default to regional placement based on account region but can request region lock via support/contract.

Q5: Subprocessors and access?
A5: We maintain a transparent subprocessor list (link below). Access to production data is restricted to a small set of operational roles; any human access is logged and requires Just-In-Time (JIT) approval for troubleshooting. Subprocessors with production-level access (hosted infra, logging, monitoring) are listed and we can provide a redacted access matrix to you.

Q6: Encryption & KMS?
A6: All data in transit uses TLS 1.2+; data at rest uses AES-256 encryption. Customers on enterprise plans may supply their own KMS keys (BYOK) for encryption of persistent artifacts. Our control plane supports integration with AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault and HSMs for Private deployments.

Supporting docs: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/sentrylane-2028-qna, SOC2: https://artifacts.redwood.com/reports/soc2-report-2028-redwood.pdf

Thanks Sergio — helpful summary. A couple of clarifications before we mark this as complete:
1) Backups: when you say "purge related items from replicas/backups on the next scheduled snapshot lifecycle (typically within 30 days)", can you provide the maximum SLA (e.g., 45/60 days) and whether emergency purge outside the snapshot window is supported?
2) Subprocessors: please provide the current list and indicate which vendors hold encryption keys or have the ability to decrypt customer artifacts.
3) SOC2: can you provide the most recent SOC2 Type II cover memo and the date range it covers?

Also, we'll need a redacted vendor access matrix for our procurement and a short statement confirming you do not use customer data to further train public models without explicit written consent.

If we can get those four items by EOD Friday it would keep our procurement timeline intact.

Internal note: looping Neha on procurement/contract questions and to pull the vendor access matrix and latest SOC2 cover memo.

Answers to your clarifications:
- Backups: Our standard recovery-oriented snapshot purge window is 30 days; we support expedited purges for production artifacts on a case-by-case basis and can pursue an emergency purge with a contractual SLA (typically 72h to initiate and completion depends on snapshot topology; we document this in the DSR/Erasures appendix we will send). We'll include a statement and maximum allowable window (we'll flag 60 days as an upper bound for rare recovery scenarios where immutable snapshots exist unless contractually overridden).
- Subprocessors: Neha, could you attach the current subprocessor list and highlight those with key-management responsibilities?
- SOC2: attaching the SOC2 cover memo and the report link; redacted artifacts will be provided via our secure share.
